title: Best Arabic catering companies in Dubai 2026
body_markdown:
Dubai's Arabic catering scene splits into four working formats: private chefs who cook Levantine and Gulf menus inside your home, restaurant banquet arms built for seated fine dining, casual street-food caterers built for volume, and bakery-led caterers built for office trays. This guide ranks the best Arabic catering companies in Dubai for 2026 by which format actually fits your guest count and occasion.


**TL;DR**

- The best Arabic catering companies in Dubai for 2026 split by format: private chef, banquet arm, casual spread, or bakery tray.
- myCHEF wins for halal-first Arabic dinners cooked inside your home, from weekly meals to full dinner parties.
- Al Nafoorah suits upscale seated Lebanese events; Zaroob fits casual, large-group Levantine spreads.
- Bateel International fits corporate gifting and gourmet Arabic hospitality trays; Mama'esh covers smaller bakery-led office lunches.
- Pick the format first — home, banquet hall, or office — then match the cuisine and guest count.


## Why this matters

Most people search for Arabic catering in Dubai by cuisine — Lebanese, Emirati, Levantine — and end up comparing companies that don't do the same job. A fine-dining Lebanese kitchen and a private chef both cook Arabic food, but one seats you in a restaurant-style setup with a fixed menu, and the other cooks inside your own kitchen on a menu built around your table, the way the private chef model at [myCHEF](https://mychef.ae/) runs across Dubai.

The mismatch shows up at booking, not at the table. A 12-person birthday dinner booked through a banquet-style caterer pays for staff and setup built for 80 covers. A 150-guest wedding booked through a bakery tray service runs out of food by the second course.

Matching format to guest count and occasion first, then picking cuisine, is what actually separates a good Arabic catering booking in Dubai in 2026 from a bad one.



## What makes the best Arabic catering companies in Dubai

- **Halal sourcing** — whether the ingredients and prep are halal-first by default, not an add-on request. See the [halal catering companies in Dubai](https://mychef.byryze.com/best-halal-catering-companies-in-dubai) breakdown for how sourcing standards differ across providers.
- **Menu breadth** — spans Levantine mezze and Gulf or Emirati mains, not just one regional style.
- **Format flexibility** — private chef, seated banquet, drop-off trays, or a street-food buffet.
- **Guest capacity** — the range the format actually handles well, from an 8-person dinner to a 300-guest gala.
- **Dietary customization** — pork-free and alcohol-free prep, plus vegetarian mezze swaps built into the menu.
- **Booking lead time** — how far ahead the menu needs locking, and how flexible last-minute changes are.

| Zaroob | Casual, large-group Levantine spreads | Street-food style Levantine menu built for volume | Casual format, not suited to formal seated service |
| Mama'esh | Smaller bakery-led office lunches | Levantine bakery and man'oushe menu | Limited hot mains and full mezze range |

## 1. myCHEF: best Arabic catering for private, halal-first dinners at home

myCHEF is a private chef and catering service in Dubai that places vetted chefs inside your kitchen for home-cooked meals, weekly meal prep, dinner parties, corporate events, and large catered celebrations. For Arabic catering, that means a chef builds a Levantine or Gulf-style menu around your guest list instead of you choosing from a fixed banquet menu. The same model covers [corporate event catering in Dubai](https://mychef.byryze.com/best-corporate-event-catering-companies-in-dubai), where offices book a private chef instead of a fixed banquet package.

**myCHEF pros:**
- Vetted, halal-first private chefs cook the menu inside your own kitchen
- Covers everything from weekly meal prep to a full dinner party or large celebration
- Menu built around guest count and dietary needs, not a fixed banquet list
- Handles both household bookings and corporate events

**myCHEF cons:**
- Booking and menu are quote-based, not a fixed public price list
- Not a walk-in order — a chef needs to be booked and briefed in advance
- Suited to home and mid-size events, not a stadium-style banquet hall setup

**Best for:** households and businesses in Dubai booking a private Arabic dinner, weekly meal prep, or a catered celebration with a vetted chef.

**Verdict: Buy** for any home-based Arabic dinner, dinner party, or corporate event in 2026 where the menu needs to be built around your table, not a fixed banquet sheet.

## 2. Bateel International: best Arabic catering for corporate gifting and gourmet spreads

Bateel International is a Gulf-based gourmet food brand known for premium dates and Arabic delicacies, with a catering and corporate gifting arm active across Dubai. It fits occasions where the spread needs to look like a luxury gift table — dates, sweets, and Arabic coffee service — rather than a full seated meal.

**Bateel International pros:**
- Strong on premium dates, sweets, and Arabic coffee presentation
- Recognized brand for corporate gifting and hospitality trays
- Works well for smaller receptions and welcome spreads

**Bateel International cons:**
- Narrower on hot mezze and full seated main courses than a dedicated caterer
- Built more for gifting-style spreads than a full sit-down Arabic dinner
- Less suited to large banquet-style events with a full multi-course menu

**Best for:** corporate welcome spreads, gifting tables, and Arabic coffee service at Dubai offices and events.

**Verdict: Buy** for a gourmet gifting table. **Skip** it if the event needs a full seated Arabic dinner with hot mains.

## 3. Al Nafoorah: best Arabic catering for upscale seated Lebanese dinners

Al Nafoorah is a Lebanese restaurant under Jumeirah Group, known for a fine-dining Lebanese menu that extends into event catering for seated dinners. It suits occasions where the format sits closer to a restaurant experience than a home dinner — plated courses, formal service, and a single-cuisine focus on Lebanese cooking.

**Al Nafoorah pros:**
- Fine-dining Lebanese kitchen with a consistent, restaurant-tested menu
- Strong fit for formal, seated event catering
- Backed by an established Dubai hospitality group

**Al Nafoorah cons:**
- Single-cuisine focus on Lebanese food rather than pan-Arab variety
- Formal fine-dining positioning suits a seated event more than a casual home gathering
- Less flexible on last-minute menu changes than a private chef booking

**Verdict: Buy** for a formal seated Lebanese dinner. **Hold** for a casual home gathering, where a private chef fits better.

## 4. Zaroob: best Arabic catering for casual, large-group Levantine spreads

Zaroob is a casual Levantine street-food chain across Dubai, known for shawarma, mezze, and grilled mains served buffet-style. Its catering arm is built for volume — large groups who want a casual, help-yourself Levantine spread rather than plated service.

**Zaroob pros:**
- Built for volume, casual Levantine spreads at large gatherings
- Familiar, crowd-pleasing menu of shawarma, mezze, and grills
- Buffet-style service scales well for bigger guest counts

**Zaroob cons:**
- Casual format doesn't suit a formal seated dinner
- Less per-guest customization than a private chef menu
- Not the fit for a small, intimate home dinner

**Best for:** large, casual gatherings and office parties that want a Levantine buffet.

**Verdict: Buy** for a big, casual Levantine spread. **Skip** it for a formal or intimate dinner.

## 5. Mama'esh: best Arabic catering for smaller bakery-led office lunches

Mama'esh is a Levantine bakery and restaurant chain in Dubai known for man'oushe and bakery-led dishes, with a catering option for smaller office lunches and casual gatherings. It works as a lighter, bakery-first alternative to a full multi-course Arabic caterer.

- Works for smaller, casual office lunches
- Lighter option than a full seated Arabic catering menu

**Mama'esh cons:**
- Limited hot mains and full mezze range compared to a dedicated caterer
- Better suited to smaller groups than a large banquet or wedding
- Not built for formal, multi-course event catering

**Best for:** smaller office lunches and casual gatherings built around bakery items.

**Verdict: Buy** for a small bakery-led lunch. **Skip** for a large formal event.
